function: Joint communication and sensing beamforming at the ground BS together with UAV movement directions (trajectories), maximizing sum-rate under a sensing SNR constraint (pp. 4-5).
system: ISAC downlink: ground BS with N=6 antennas, M=4 single-antenna UAVs flying at 80 m, one moving target, LoS air-ground channels; carrier frequency not stated (pp. 3-4, 9-10).
method: DeepLSC: DDPG actor-critic with GRU layers, constrained noise-exploration policy, hierarchical experience replay and symmetric (permutation) experience augmentation; online reinforcement learning with penalty reward (pp. 5-9).
data_channel: Own simulator, no dataset: LoS air-ground channel with path loss exponent 3.2, L0=-30 dB at 1 m, Gauss-Markov target mobility; online interaction over 5000 episodes (pp. 4, 10).
test_conditions: Online learning in each setting (5000 episodes); robustness runs vary M from 2 to 5 and T from 40 to 70; no train-then-test on unseen settings (pp. 10-12).
baselines: Own variants DeepLSC-CNE, DeepLSC-CER, DeepLSC-w, and AC2 (standard actor-critic with the same policy and reward); no non-learned baseline (pp. 10-11).
metrics: Communication sum-rate (average over previous 200 episodes), average sensing SNR, flight-mission satisfaction, and episodes to converge (pp. 10-12).
q1_support: p. 4: "the air-ground communication links are dominated by the LoS channel"; p. 10: "The path loss exponent is 3.2". Custom LoS model; no 3GPP model, dataset or measurement is used.
q2_support: p. 11: "against different numbers of UAVs, in which M increases from 2 to 5". Each setting is its own online-learning run (the output size depends on M, p. 6); no trained model is tested on an unseen setting.
q3_support: p. 10: "In the simulation, the following schemes are considered": DeepLSC, DeepLSC-CNE, DeepLSC-CER, DeepLSC-w and AC2 are all DRL; a learned baseline exists but no non-learned method is compared.
q4_support: p. 10: "The GRU and FC layers of DeepLSC contain 128 neurons" is only the layer width; no complexity order, FLOPs, parameter count or runtime is reported, and convergence in episodes (p. 11) is training speed.
q5_support: p. 9: "on Python 3.6 simulation platform, where the Keras library [44] builds all DNN models"; no code or data link appears in the paper, and channels come from its own simulator.
notes: Identity checked: PDF is arXiv v3 (2 Jan 2025, p. 1) of 'Integrated Sensing and Communications for Low-Altitude Economy: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach', matching the DOI; it predates the journal version, so tables may differ. Passes above_phy because the agent learns communication and sensing beamforming jointly with UAV trajectories (p. 5). Area 6 rather than 5 is a judgment to confirm: the links are air-ground to UAVs (p. 4) and the tie-break puts 6 before 5, but the paper calls the setting 'terrestrial ISAC' (p. 2); if the reviewer reads the links as terrestrial, area 5. q2: Sections V-C and V-D vary M and T as robustness checks, but each is a separate online-learning run, which counts as retraining. q3: AC2 is a standard actor-critic on the same problem, but all five schemes are learned; the related work only discusses conventional optimization (p. 2) without comparing it.
